question.text:
Arrange the following functions in increasing order of asymptotic growth:

$f_1(n) = \log(n^n)$

$f_2(n) = (\log n)^n$

$f_3(n) = \log(n^{6006})$

$f_4(n) = (\log n)^{6006}$

$f_5(n) = \log\log(6006n)$
 

  1. $f_5(n)< f_3(n)< f_4(n)< f_1(n)< f_2(n)$

  2. $f_5(n)< f_3(n)< f_1(n)< f_4(n)< f_2(n)$

  3. $f_3(n)< f_5(n)< f_4(n)< f_1(n)< f_2(n)$

  4. $f_5(n)< f_4(n)< f_3(n)< f_1(n)< f_2(n)$
question.subject: Algorithms

question.text:
Suppose $g(n) \in \Theta(n^3)$.

Which of the following statements are always true?

  • $\text{S1}:$ $g(n) \in O(n^3)$
     
  • $\text{S2}:$ $g(n) \in \Theta(n)$
     
  • $\text{S3}:$ $g(n) \in \Omega(n)$
     
  1. $\text{S1}$ only
     
  2. $\text{S1}$ and $\text{S3}$ only
     
  3. $\text{S2}$ and $\text{S3}$ only
     
  4. $\text{S1}$, $\text{S2}$ and $\text{S3}$
question.subject: Algorithms

question.text:
Suppose we have three functions $f(n)$, $g(n)$, and $h(n)$ such that:

$f(n) \in O(g(n))\qquad$ and $\qquad g(n) \in O(h(n))$

Which of the following statements are guaranteed to be true?

$\text{S1}:$ $f(n) \in O(h(n))$

$\text{S2}:$ $h(n) \in \Omega(f(n))$

$\text{S3}:$ $f(n) + g(n) \in O(g(n))$

$\text{S4}:$ $f(n)\cdot g(n) \in O(h(n))$

$\text{S5}:$ If we also know that $f(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$, then $g(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$

  1. $\text{S1}$, $\text{S2}$ and $\text{S3}$ only
     
  2. $\text{S1}$, $\text{S2}$, $\text{S3}$ and $\text{S5}$ only
     
  3. $\text{S1}$, $\text{S4}$ and $\text{S5}$ only
     
  4. $\text{S1}$, $\text{S2}$, $\text{S3}$, $\text{S4}$ and $\text{S5}$
question.subject: Algorithms

question.text:
Arrange the following functions in increasing order of asymptotic growth:

  • $f_1(n) = n^{0.999999}\log n$
     
  • $f_2(n) = 10000000n$
     
  • $f_3(n) = 1.000001^n$
     
  • $f_4(n) = n^2$

 

  1. $f_1(n)< f_2(n)< f_4(n)< f_3(n)$
     
  2. $f_1(n)< f_4(n)< f_2(n)< f_3(n)$
     
  3. $f_2(n)<f_1(n)< f_4(n)< f_3(n)$
     
  4. $f_1(n)< f_2(n)< f_3(n)< f_4(n)$
